Read New Zealand National Soils Database survey exports

Source: R/nsd.R
read_nsd_pedons.Rd

Reads the survey exports of the New Zealand National Soils Database (NSD, Manaaki Whenua - Landcare Research), as the National Soil Data Repository (NSDR) serves them (one zip of relational CSV tables per survey), into PedonRecord objects. The tables are read in memory from the zips (or from unzipped folders); nothing is written to disk.

Usage

read_nsd_pedons(
  path,
  absent_unless_recorded = TRUE,
  old_notation = c("translate", "asis"),
  classified_only = FALSE,
  accessed = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

path

One or more NSD survey zips, folders holding the unzipped CSV tables of a survey, or folders of either.

absent_unless_recorded

If TRUE (default), a described horizon (one with a matrix colour) with no mottle record, in a survey that records mottles, has none, unless its designation marks gleying.

old_notation

"translate" (default) or "asis": how designations in the older New Zealand notation are read (see Details).

classified_only

If TRUE, only profiles with an NZSC class.

accessed

Optional date the exports were downloaded, kept in the site and the citation.

verbose

Print the number of profiles read per survey.

Value

A named list of PedonRecord objects (names are the NSD site identifiers).

Details

Each pedon carries the field description (designations, depths, boundary, moist Munsell colour, field texture, strength, failure, stickiness, plasticity, cementation, mottles, structure, clay coats and the colour of coatings, pans, roots) and the laboratory results of its samples (carbon, nitrogen, pH in water, KCl, CaCl2 and NaF, P retention, CEC and exchangeable cations, base saturation, KCl-extractable Al, oxalate, dithionite and pyrophosphate Fe and Al, particle size, bulk density, volcanic glass in the sand, stones, CaCO3, EC of a 1:5 extract, water at 1500 kPa, COLE), with the NSD table and column of every value in the provenance. Codes are decoded through the survey's cl_concept table. The site holds the surveyor's classes: reference_nzsc (the NZSC code, e.g. "MOT", recoded to the 4th edition where the 4th edition renamed it), reference_nzsc_name, the order, group and subgroup codes (reference_nzsc_order, _group, _subgroup), the record as written (reference_nzsc_raw), reference_usda (the Soil Taxonomy order of the recorded name), reference_usda_grtgroup, reference_usda_subgroup, the NZ Genetic class and series; and the drainage class, the parent material (the soil note "PARENT ROCK"), the landform, whether the land is drained, the mean annual air temperature, latitude and longitude (from NZTM2000), the licence and the citation (nsd_citation). The header of R/nsd.R lists every reading.

Designations: the NSD gives many horizons a designation in the current notation (designation_fao), which is read (an FAO H master as the New Zealand O); the others keep the surveyor's designation, often in the older New Zealand notation (Taylor and Pohlen 1962). With old_notation = "translate", (B) is read as Bw, the suffixes fe, ca and cs as s, k and y, an upper-case G suffix as g, and digits written between the master and its suffixes are moved to the end (B2g as Bg2). A2 is read as E, with its subdivisions and suffixes (A21 as E1, A2g as Eg). The old master G (a gley horizon) is read as Bg when a B horizon lies below it in the profile, otherwise as Cg (GC as BCg or Cg); the old master D (the substratum) as C, its prefixes and suffixes kept (BD as BC, DG as Cg) except its old suffixes r and n, which are not read (Dr and Dn as C; the NSD's own conversions give them as Cu, C, Bt or Cm). A cemented sesquioxidic B written Bms is read as Bfm (a placic horizon) when 10 mm or less thick and as Bsm (an ortstein-pan) when thicker, as the NZSC Diagnostics define them. The provenance keeps the recorded designation and what it was read as.

Structure: the older ped term nut (not a shape of Milne et al. 1995) is granular or polyhedral, one of the two (NZ Soil Description Handbook 2024, Note 12.1). It is kept in structure_type_one_of with structure_type empty: classify_nzsc4 reads a criterion under each shape, and the other keys read the shape as not recorded. The older strength words moderately weak, moderately firm and moderately strong (of the Taylor and Pohlen 1962 scale) are not read.

Parent material: the soil note PARENT ROCK is also the layer_origin of each horizon whose origin is not recorded (the NSD exports record none per horizon). A note naming a sequence of materials ("loess over outwash gravels") is split by the profile's lithologic groups (2C, IIC) when its parts are as many; otherwise it stays the site's parent_material only.

The NSD records no field reactive-aluminium (NaF) test, Childs' test, sensitivity, fluidity, packing or Ksat, which the NZSC key reads; the laboratory pH in NaF is kept in ph_naf.

References

Manaaki Whenua - Landcare Research (2020). National Soils Database (NSD). doi:10.26060/95m4-cz25 . Milne, J.D.G., Clayden, B., Singleton, P.L. and Wilson, A.D. (1995). Soil Description Handbook. Manaaki Whenua Press.

See also

benchmark_nsd, classify_nzsc4.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
peds <- read_nsd_pedons("path/to/nsd/surveys")
b <- benchmark_nsd(peds, level = "order")
b$accuracy
} # }
